tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kits
tips.text: To strip old paint from plastic kits, use Tamiya Extra Thin Cement. Apply liberally to the surface, let it soak for 1-2 minutes, then gently scrape off the softened paint with a wood toothpick or scribe. For stubborn areas, use a sharp hobby knife. Once paint is removed, clean the surface with alcohol to prepare for priming.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: To repair broken photo-etch parts, use CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue. Apply a tiny dot with a toothpick or needle to the joint, let it dry, then press the parts together firmly. For extra strength, apply a small amount of Vallejo Acrylic Thinner to the joint before gluing. Once dry, hide the repair with Vallejo Metal Color paint or appropriate weathering techniques.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog an airbrush, first disassemble and clean with warm water and mild detergent. If clog persists, soak the tip and needle in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15-30 minutes, then scrub with a soft toothbrush. For severe clogs, use a pin vise to carefully widen the tip opening. Reassemble, test with water, then paint to ensure proper functioning.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Parts
tips.text: To straighten warped plastic parts, immerse them in warm water for 30 seconds, then gently bend them back into shape using tweezers or pliers. Let them dry flat on a towel. For severe warping, use a hot air gun to heat the part, then gently bend it back into shape while still warm.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: To prevent frost from forming on paint when using rattle cans in cold weather, warm the can in warm water for 10-15 minutes before use. Shake well and test spray on a scrap piece before painting your model. Always paint in a well-ventilated area and avoid direct sunlight.
